newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka opposition seeks holy help for fair polls.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka opposition seeks holy help for fair polls.

text.p: Sri Lanka's main opposition United National Party (UNP) will seek divine intervention to keep future elections free and fair, party officials said on Tuesday.
The party will begin a campaign on Sunday to encourage people to tie yellow ribbons at Buddhist temples, churches and other places.
Attached to the ribbons will be circular pieces of wood inscribed with the words "For a free and fair election".
Sinhalese Buddhists, who form 74 percent of Sri Lanka's 18 million population, observe a similar practice to seek Lord Buddha's blessing.
"Election observers have reported that there has been mass scale rigging at local polls (in March). This will be a continuing feature," UNP leader Ranil Wickremasinghe told a news conference.
"This is not a UNP campaign, this is a campaign for the people," he said.
The UNP's 17-year rule ended in 1994 when the ruling People's Alliance was voted into power.
